acceptanceCriteria: The document maps entry points (CLI/MCP), observation/snapshot capture, Contract/policy/evidence validation, governance judgment, lifecycle transitions, command execution/scheduling, status/Outcome/human-decision projection, and persistence/recovery to their current authoritative source and owning file/function, with file:line citations.

The document cites concrete, line-referenced examples of duplicate fact reads across functions, functions that mix observation+decision+persistence, and any circular or one-directional dependency between lib.rs and governance_controls.rs/project_governance.rs.

The document names what is already well-separated and reusable as-is (e.g. RepositorySnapshot, RuntimeContext, the pure validators in governance_controls.rs, the capability-scoped file-I/O primitives) so later Work Items build on them instead of duplicating them.

For each of P1-B, P2-A, P2-B, P2-C, and P3, the document states the specific problem, the target responsibility boundary, the concrete compatibility risk, and how it would be verified -- without prescribing a full interface design.

The document states plainly where PhysicalSingleFlightCoordinator and the verification DAG/scheduler live relative to governance-decision code (crate-level separation already exists), as the factual basis for the P3 Work Item.
goal: Produce a reference document giving every subsequent architecture Work Item (P1-B observation context, P2-A lifecycle/storage extraction, P2-B state types, P2-C multi-file consistency, P3 physical execution boundary) a shared, cited factual basis: which layer currently owns each fact, where duplicate reads and mixed responsibilities exist, what is already well-separated and reusable, and for each candidate refactor a concrete problem statement, target boundary, compatibility risk, and verification method.
intent: Document the current responsibility and dependency boundaries of the AI Cockpit Runtime before further architecture refactoring: crates/cockpit-repository/src/lib.rs is 18220 lines and mixes observation (file/git reads), governance decision, lifecycle coordination, evidence storage, and persistence inside single functions across most of its functional clusters. This Work Item is fact-finding and planning only; it does not change any code.
outOfScope: Any code change; this Work Item documents current behavior only
Designing new trait/Port interfaces in detail; only naming candidate boundaries and open questions
